svg.title: A nurse in the emergency department is caring for a 12-year-old child who has ingested bleach. Which of the following statements by the nurse indicates an understanding of this ingestion?
svg.desc: A liquid corrosive does not stick, so more is swallowed and it coats as it goes — larger area of contact, more extensive esophageal and often gastric injury. A solid or granule adheres to the mouth and upper esophagus, which hurts at once and tends to limit how much goes down. The other three are the classic traps: a clean mouth proves nothing , because oral and pharyngeal burns do not reliably accompany esophageal ones — children who looked fine have had severe injury on endoscopy. Neutralizing is never done : a weak acid on an alkali is an exothermic reaction, adding a thermal burn to the chemical one. And activated charcoal is contraindicated for corrosives — it does not bind them and it coats the mucosa so the damage cannot be seen on endoscopy. Airway first, keep them NPO, endoscopy stages the burn.
